summary: This roadmap plans the final part of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni's proof that abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular (Publ. IHÉS 2021, arXiv:1812.09269v3): the Taylor–Wiles–Calegari–Geraghty argument of §§7.7–7.13 in defect 0 and 1 on higher Hida complexes, the gluing by doubling, analytic continuation and étale descent of §8 giving the modularity lifting theorem (Theorem 8.4.1), the p–q switch giving potential modularity of challenging surfaces and potential automorphy of all abelian surfaces with the Hasse–Weil conjecture for genus two curves (§9), and the modularity results of §10 (ordinary surfaces, fixed 3-torsion via the odd-theta cover of the Burkhardt quartic, infinitely many modular surfaces over Q, the paramodular conjecture). It also owns the Galois representations of ordinary parallel weight 2 forms (Theorem 1.8.17 of the 2025 sequel) and the local seed curves at 3 (its Corollary 9.3.6 and Lemma 9.3.7). Hilbert–Siegel varieties, higher Hida and Coleman theory, integral coherent Hecke complexes, GSp_4 local Langlands and open image theorems are imported from their owners; four of those owners are undesigned Part IIs and the Hilbert–Siegel higher Hida/Coleman statements are not yet in HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, so the imports are recorded as Part II requests at the parent stages. Independent review corrected conventions, negative tests, local seed realization and proof dependencies. Defect-one flatness, the switch polarization type and the explicit quaternionic certificates remain genuine gaps; AP.3–AP.7 are partial and the review requires changes. No mathematical implementation is claimed.

nodes.title: The GSp_4-valued compatible system of an abelian surface
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian surface over a number field F and l a prime. Put ρ_{A,l} := H^1_ét(A_{F̄}, Q̄_l), a continuous four-dimensional representation of G_F, and 𝓡_A := (ρ_{A,l})_l. A polarization λ of A induces, through its Weil pairing, a G_F-equivariant perfect alternating pairing on H^1_ét(A_{F̄}, Q̄_l) with values in Q̄_l(−1); in a symplectic basis ρ_{A,l} takes values in GSp_4(Q̄_l) with multiplier ν∘ρ_{A,l} = ε_l^{−1}, and its GSp_4(Q̄_l)-conjugacy class does not depend on λ. A family of GSp_4-valued representations is called a weakly (resp. strictly) compatible system when the underlying GL_4-valued family is; no compatibility between the symplectic forms is demanded, since every system considered has multiplier the inverse cyclotomic character. The residual representation ρ̄_{A,p}: G_F → GSp_4(F̄_p) is the dual of the Galois module A[p](F̄).
hypotheses: F is a number field (totally real in every use from AP.1 on); A is an abelian variety of dimension 2 over F.
Geometric Frobenius normalization: for v ∤ l of good reduction, ρ_{A,l}(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial X^4 − a_1X^3 + a_2X^2 − q_v a_1 X + q_v^2 with a_1, a_2 ∈ Z independent of l.

For the residual symplectic representation on the dual of the actual p-torsion, fix a polarization of degree prime to p. Without this hypothesis use a stable symplectic lattice and specify its semisimplified reduction; do not silently identify every lattice reduction with A[p]^∨.
proofSteps: Construct ρ_{A,l} from the étale Tate module (A4) as the Q̄_l-dual of V_lA ⊗ Q̄_l, with its G_F action and continuity.

Use the Weil pairing attached to a polarization (A3); it is alternating, perfect after inverting l, and G_F acts on its target through the cyclotomic character, which on H^1 gives the multiplier ε_l^{−1}.

Independence of λ: ρ_{A,l} is semisimple (Faltings, R28.4), and a semisimple GSp_4-valued representation is determined up to GSp_4-conjugacy by its GL_4-valued representation and its multiplier (BCGP Lemma 2.1.3, owned by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7).

Strict compatibility and purity of 𝓡_A are BCGP Proposition 2.8.1, imported from NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5; the compatible-system API is PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5:operations.

nodes.title: Automorphic compatible systems over a number field
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and 𝓡 a strictly compatible system of n-dimensional representations of G_K. 𝓡 is automorphic if there is an automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_K) such that (1) Π = Π_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ Π_r is an isobaric sum of C-algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations Π_i of GL_{n_i}(A_K); (2) the fixed field M_Π ⊂ C of {σ ∈ Aut(C) : σΠ^∞ ≅ Π^∞} is a number field; (3) for every finite place v of K, WD_v(𝓡) ≅ ⊕_i rec(Π_{i,v} ⊗ |det|_v^{(1−n_i)/2}). No condition is imposed at the infinite places. 𝓡 is potentially automorphic if 𝓡|_{G_L} is automorphic for some finite extension L/K. When 𝓡 is automorphic with Π, the completed function Λ_Π(𝓡,s) := L(𝓡,s)∏_{v|∞}L_v(Π,s) continues meromorphically to C and satisfies Λ_Π(𝓡,s) = ε(Π)N(Π)^{−s}Λ_Π(𝓡^∨,1−s).
hypotheses: rec is the local Langlands correspondence for GL_m over finite extensions of Q_p, with full Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameters; WD_v(𝓡) is the common Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation of the strictly compatible system at v.
The coefficient field of Π is computed from its finite part Π^∞.
proofSteps: Isobaric sums and strong multiplicity one for isobaric representations are imported from the automorphic spectral owner (AS.4).

Condition (2) follows from (3) and strong multiplicity one; it is kept separate because it is the condition expected to follow from (1) alone. In the two cases used it holds: Π regular algebraic (Clozel), and Π the transfer to GL_4 of a cuspidal GSp_4 representation of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 (Blasius–Harris–Ramakrishnan), as recorded in Remark 9.1.2.
The functional equation (9.1.5) is the Godement–Jacquet functional equation for the Π_i (AL.2), multiplied over i.

nodes.title: Automorphic and potentially automorphic abelian varieties
nodes.statement: An abelian variety A over a number field K is automorphic if 𝓡_A is automorphic, and potentially automorphic if 𝓡_A|_{G_L} is automorphic for some finite extension L/K. If A is automorphic through a Π of one of the two forms (a) Π_i regular algebraic, or (b) K totally real, Π cuspidal and the transfer to GL_4 of a cuspidal GSp_4 representation of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, then the archimedean factors and conductor of Π agree with those of 𝓡_A, so Λ_Π(𝓡_A,s) = Λ(𝓡_A,s) and Λ(𝓡_A,s) has meromorphic continuation and the expected functional equation.
hypotheses: K is a number field and A/K an abelian variety; 𝓡_A = (H^1_ét(A_{K̄}, Q̄_l))_l.
proofSteps: Unfold the definition through automorphic-compatible-system.

Remark 9.1.7: in cases (a) and (b) the Gamma factors L_v(Π,s), v|∞, are those of the Hodge structure of A and the conductor N(Π) is the Artin conductor of 𝓡_A, because the conductor respects local Langlands; so the two functional equations (2.8.5) and (9.1.5) coincide.

nodes.title: Modular and potentially modular GSp_4-representations and abelian surfaces
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real. A continuous ρ: G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) is modular if there is a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 such that WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) for every finite place v of F; in particular ρ^{ss} ≅ ρ_{π,p}; if ρ is semisimple then ρ ≅ ρ_{π,p}. ρ is potentially modular if ρ|_{G_{F'}} is modular for some finite Galois extension F'/F of totally real fields. An abelian surface A/F is modular (resp. potentially modular) if ρ_{A,p} is, for some prime p; this does not depend on p. Both versions of the paper print WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}}) where WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}) is meant; the definition is used in the corrected form.
hypotheses: Parallel weight 2: at every real place π_v lies in the archimedean L-packet of weight (2,2) (holomorphic and generic limits of discrete series), in the conventions of BCGP §2.6, owned by the GSp_4 Part II of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions.
rec_{GT,p} is Gan–Takeda's local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 transported to Q̄_p, normalized as in BCGP §2.3.
proofSteps: The unramified matches and Chebotarev–Brauer–Nesbitt identify ρ^{ss} with ρ_{π,p} as GL_4 representations; when ρ is semisimple, Lemma 2.1.3 (G7) upgrades this to GSp_4 with the specified multiplier. No isomorphism with a potentially nonsplit ρ follows just from its traces.

Independence of p for abelian surfaces: 𝓡_A is strictly compatible (R11.5), so the Weil–Deligne representations of ρ_{A,p'} at every finite v agree with those of ρ_{A,p}; the Galois representations attached to π at p' are compatible with π at all v.
Remark 9.1.9: when the transfer of π to GL_4 is cuspidal (π of general type), a modular A is automorphic in the sense of Definition 9.1.6, case (b) of Remark 9.1.2.

nodes.title: Galois representations of ordinary parallel weight 2 forms on GSp_4
nodes.statement: Let F^+ be totally real, p a prime splitting completely in F^+, and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_{F^+}) of parallel weight 2 (algebraic of weight (1,1;2) at every real place, with π_∞ a non-degenerate limit of discrete series) and central character |·|^2, ordinary at every place above p. Then there is a continuous semisimple ρ_{π,p}: G_{F^+} → GSp_4(Q̄_p) such that (i) ν∘ρ_{π,p} = ε^{−1}; (ii) for every finite v ∤ p, WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F^+_v}})^{ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2})^{ss}; (iii) for every v | p there are potentially unramified characters α_v, β_v of G_{F^+_v} with ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F^+_v}} conjugate to an upper triangular representation with diagonal (α_v, β_v, β_v^{−1}ε^{−1}, α_v^{−1}ε^{−1}), the diagonal being read off from the ordinary p-stabilization of π_v. No hypothesis p > 2, no residual image condition and no distinctness of the ordinary Hecke parameters is assumed; de Rhamness at p is not asserted. The statement depends on Arthur's classification for GSp_4 through the regular weight input, whose conditional status is carried as recorded at ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.0 and ML.4.
hypotheses: F^+ totally real; p splits completely in F^+.
π cuspidal, of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, ordinary at every v | p.
Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp_4 (BCGP18 §1.4.1), in the conditional form recorded by ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions.
proofSteps: π^∞ occurs in the interior coherent cohomology of the Hilbert–Siegel variety (Harris; imported with the coherent Hecke complexes).

π defines a point x of the equidimensional higher Coleman eigenvariety, which dominates weight space and in which classical points of regular algebraic weight are Zariski dense near x (Boxer–Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory, Theorem 1.4.3; HigherHidaAndColemanTheory E6). Choose an affinoid neighbourhood, inside an ordinary component when π is ordinary.

At the dense regular points the Galois representations of regular weight (BCGP25 Theorem 1.8.13 = BCGP18 Theorem 2.7.1, owned by the GSp_4 Part II of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) give GSp_4-valued pseudocharacters (the connected reductive pseudocharacters of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0); interpolate them over the affinoid (IHG.4, extended to affinoid coefficients) and specialize at x to obtain, by reconstruction over Q̄_p (IHG.1; V. Lafforgue, Quast), a semisimple ρ_{π,p}.

Reconstruct inside GSp_4 from the reductive pseudocharacter, including its fixed multiplier; this supplies a nondegenerate alternating form. The mere occurrence of ε^{−1} in ∧^2ρ is insufficient to prove nondegeneracy. Interpolate semisimplified Weil–Deligne parameters away from p and the ordinary filtration on the ordinary component (Boxer–Pilloni Theorem 1.4.8) to obtain (ii) and (iii).

sources.locator: Theorem 1.8.17 with (1.8.18)–(1.8.19), Definition 1.8.16 and Remark 1.8.15, §1.8, pp. 13–14
sources.match: States the existence of a semisimple GSp_4-valued representation for an ordinary weight 2 representation over a totally real field in which p splits, with multiplier ε^{−1}, semisimplified local–global compatibility away from p and the ordinary triangular shape at p, and sketches its proof by interpolation over the Boxer–Pilloni eigenvariety.
The 2018 paper constructs the same representation in parallel weight 2 under extra residual hypotheses, by the Hida-family route of Theorem 7.9.4.

acceptance: (i) gives multiplier ε^{−1}, which Hypothesis 7.8.1(5) and Hypothesis 7.13.1(6) use to compare ρ̄_{π,p} with ρ̄.
For π of general type with ρ_{π,p} pure, the semisimplified compatibility upgrades to full Frobenius-semisimple compatibility (BCGP25 Remark 1.8.20), which is how Corollary 8.2.2 matches monodromy.

nodes.title: The standing hypotheses on ρ̄ and the auxiliary place v_0
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p ≥ 3 a prime splitting completely in F, S_p the places above p, k a finite field of characteristic p and ρ̄: G_F → GSp_4(k) absolutely irreducible. Hypothesis 7.7.1 asks: (1) ρ̄ is vast and tidy; (2) ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for v ∈ S_p; (3) there is a finite set R of finite places disjoint from S_p such that for v ∈ R, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is trivial and q_v ≡ 1 mod p (mod 9 if p = 3), and ρ̄ is unramified outside S_p ∪ R. Hypothesis 7.8.1 adds an ordinary cuspidal automorphic π of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄, π_v^{Iw(v)} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R ∪ S_p and π_v unramified otherwise. Under either hypothesis fix an auxiliary place v_0 ∉ R ∪ S_p, absolutely unramified, with q_{v_0} ≢ 1 mod p, no two eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_{v_0}) of ratio q_{v_0}, and residue characteristic > 5; put S = R ∪ S_p ∪ {v_0} and ψ = ε^{−1}.
hypotheses: p ≥ 3; F totally real and p totally split in F.

Vast, tidy and enormous are the residual-image conditions of BCGP Definitions 7.5.2, 7.5.6 and 7.5.11, owned by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7; p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary is Definition 7.3.1, owned by LocalGaloisDeformationRings.
proofSteps: Existence of v_0: tidiness of ρ̄(G_F) and Chebotarev give a positive density of v with the four properties; 'absolutely unramified' is needed for Lemma 7.8.3 and is stated explicitly in §7.13(8).

Local duality gives H^2(F_{v_0}, ad ρ̄) ≅ H^0(F_{v_0}, ad ρ̄(1))^∨, which vanishes by the eigenvalue-ratio condition; then every lift of ρ̄|_{G_{F_{v_0}}} is unramified (Proposition 7.4.2, LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2).
Hypothesis 7.8.1 implies Hypothesis 7.7.1 by inclusion of its clauses.

acceptance: For p = 3 and F = Q, 19 and 37 may lie in R, while 7 may not (7 ≢ 1 mod 9).

nodes.title: The global deformation problems S_χ^{I,𝔠} and S_{χ,Q}^{I,𝔠}
nodes.statement: Assume Hypothesis 7.7.1 with S = R ∪ S_p ∪ {v_0}. Choose I ⊆ S_p (I^c = S_p ∖ I); for v ∈ R a pair χ_v = (χ_{v,1}, χ_{v,2}) of characters O_{F_v}^× → O^× trivial mod λ; for v ∈ I, Λ_v = O[[O_{F_v}^×(p)]] with universal character θ_v, and for v ∈ I^c, Λ_v = O[[O_{F_v}^×(p)^2]] with θ_{v,1}, θ_{v,2}; and 𝔠 = (𝔠_v)_{v∈S_p} with 𝔠_v ∈ {ᾱ_v, β̄_v}. Then S_χ^{I,𝔠} is the problem of deformations of ρ̄ with multiplier ε^{−1}, unramified outside S, over the coefficient ring Λ_I = ⊗̂_{v∈S_p}Λ_v, with local conditions D_v^P (v ∈ I, Klingen-parabolic ordinary), D_v^{B,𝔠_v} (v ∈ I^c, Borel ordinary with the unit eigenvalue lifting 𝔠_v), D_v^{χ_v} (v ∈ R, Ihara avoidance) and D_{v_0}^□ (unrestricted). For a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q, (ᾱ_{v,1},…,ᾱ_{v,4})_{v∈Q}), S_{χ,Q}^{I,𝔠} is the same problem with ramification allowed in S_Q = S ∪ Q and the unrestricted condition at v ∈ Q; it is a problem over Λ_I[Δ_Q]. Neither problem depends on 𝔠_v for v ∈ I.
hypotheses: The local problems D_v^P, D_v^{B,𝔠_v} (§7.3) and D_v^χ (§7.4.5) and their rings are owned by LocalGaloisDeformationRings; Taylor–Wiles data and Δ_Q (§7.6) by GlobalGaloisDeformations.
The paper prints the Taylor–Wiles datum with n eigenvalues; there are four.
proofSteps: Assemble the global problem from the local problems with the formalism of global deformation problems with fixed multiplier (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.3, G7) and Λ_I-coefficients from the completed group rings (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1).

Representability of R_{S_χ^{I,𝔠}} and R_{S_{χ,Q}^{I,𝔠}} follows from absolute irreducibility of ρ̄ (R04.2); the Λ_I[Δ_Q]-algebra structure comes from the inertia action at v ∈ Q (Lemma 7.4.4 and the O[Δ_v]-structure, LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2).
Independence of 𝔠_v for v ∈ I: the Klingen-parabolic condition does not choose an eigenvalue.

nodes.title: Weights of Λ_I, classical weights, κ_2 and κ_reg
nodes.statement: Fix I ⊆ S_p and Λ_I = ⊗̂_{v∈S_p}Λ_v. A weight is an O-algebra homomorphism κ: Λ_I → O; it corresponds to characters θ_{v,1}, θ_{v,2}: I_{F_v} → O^× (v ∈ S_p) with trivial reduction and θ_{v,1} = θ_{v,2} for v ∈ I; 𝔭_κ = ker κ. κ is classical if there are integers k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2 with θ_{v,1} = ε^{(k_v+l_v)/2−2}, θ_{v,2} = ε^{(k_v−l_v)/2}, and l_v = 2 for v ∈ I; then k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 or p+1 mod 2(p−1), and ω^κ is the automorphic vector bundle of weight (k_v, l_v)_v. κ_2 is the classical weight k_v = l_v = 2 for all v. For I = ∅, κ_reg is a sufficiently regular classical weight, for example θ_{v,1} = ε^{2N(p−1)}, θ_{v,2} = ε^{N(p−1)} for N large, chosen so that the classicality and automorphic-description theorems apply in weight κ_reg.
hypotheses: Λ_v as in the deformation problems; ε is the p-adic cyclotomic character restricted to inertia.
proofSteps: Weights are points of Spec Λ_I, and characters of inertia with trivial reduction correspond to homomorphisms of the completed group rings (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1).
The congruence k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 or p+1 mod 2(p−1) is the condition that both ε-powers have trivial reduction, i.e. are divisible by p−1.
κ_reg is fixed so that Theorem 3.10.1 (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes) and Theorem 6.6.5 (higher Hida/Coleman comparison) apply (Remark 7.8.9).

Let Q_v(X) = X^4 − T_{v,1}X^3 + (q_vT_{v,2} + (q_v^3+q_v)T_{v,0})X^2 − q_v^3T_{v,0}T_{v,1}X + q_v^6T_{v,0}^2 ∈ T̃[X], and m̃^{an} ⊂ T̃ the maximal ideal of ρ̄ (λ ∈ m̃^{an}, det(X − ρ̄(Frob_v)) ≡ Q_v(X)). nodes.title: Proposition 7.8.11: freeness in defect 0 and balancedness in defect 1
nodes.statement: Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1, and let χ, 𝔠 and a Taylor–Wiles datum Q be as above. Then (1) M^{χ,∅,𝔠,Q} is a finite free Λ_∅[Δ_Q]-module; (2) if #I = 1, M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} is a balanced Λ_I[Δ_Q]-module: it has a presentation by a square matrix over Λ_I[Δ_Q], equivalently it is the H^0 of a perfect complex of amplitude [0,1] with Euler characteristic 0 (BCGP §2.10).
hypotheses: p ≥ 3 (used to split off the p-part of the class group acting on components).
proofSteps: The complex M^{•,I}_{K_1^p(Q)} is perfect over Λ_I of amplitude [0, #I] (Theorem 4.6.1). By Proposition 7.8.10 (owned by the Hilbert–Siegel Part II), the cover X_{K_pK_1^p(Q,R)} → X_{K_pK_0^p(Q,R)} of toroidal compactifications is finite étale with group ∏_{v∈Q∪R}T(k(v)), so the complex is represented by flat complete Λ_I[∏T(k(v))]-modules, and the semi-local form of Lemma 4.6.22 makes it perfect over Λ_I[∏T(k(v))] of amplitude [0, #I]; hence its χ-part is perfect over Λ_I[Δ_Q].
Localization at m̃^{I,𝔠} preserves perfectness and amplitude.
Central character: with C = F^×∖A_F^×/U = C_p ⊕ C^p, M̃^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} ≅ M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} ⊗_O O[C_p] because C^p acts through eigenvalues fixed mod m and C_p permutes components freely; this uses p ≠ 2.

Part (1) follows since the amplitude is [0,0]. For (2), by Lemma 2.10.2 it suffices that the localized complex of amplitude [0,1] has Euler characteristic 0, which is checked modulo primes of Λ_I using Theorem 6.6.5 and Corollary 3.10.5 (in regular weight, H^1 and H^0 of the localized coherent cohomology have the same dimension when the defect is one).

nodes.title: Proposition 7.9.1: the doubling surjections M^{χ,I,𝔠} ⊗ Λ_{I'} → M^{χ,I',𝔠}
nodes.statement: Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1. For I ⊆ I' ⊆ S_p let Λ_I → Λ_{I'} be the surjection cutting out θ_{v,1} = θ_{v,2} for v ∈ I'. For each choice 𝔠 there are natural surjections M^{χ,I,𝔠} ⊗_{Λ_I} Λ_{I'} → M^{χ,I',𝔠} and M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} ⊗_{Λ_I} Λ_{I'} → M^{χ,I',𝔠,Q}. They commute with all Hecke operators away from I' ∖ I, and for v ∈ I' ∖ I they commute with U_{v,0}, U_{v,2} and intertwine U_{v,1} on the source with the lift 𝔠̃_v of 𝔠_v on the target. Writing 𝔠'_v for the other unit eigenvalue, (U_{v,1} − 𝔠̃'_v)(U_{v,1} − 𝔠̃_v) = 0 (7.9.2).
hypotheses: Hypothesis 7.8.1 (in particular ᾱ_v ≠ β̄_v for v ∈ S_p).
proofSteps: Reduce to I' = I ∪ {v}. The map is τ∘U_{v,1} − 𝔠̃'_v∘τ, with τ induced by restriction from the Klingen-level ordinary locus at v to the Iwahori-level one (𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli(p^∞)} ⊂ 𝔛^{G_1,I'}_{K,Kli(p^∞)}).
Intertwining: Lemma 4.5.17 gives U_{v,1}(U_{Kli(v),1} − U_{v,1}) = U_{v,2} on the ordinary locus at v, i.e. (7.9.2), and Hensel's lemma separates the two roots.

Surjectivity: by Nakayama and Lemma 7.8.5(1) it reduces to injectivity on the special fibre of the weight 2 map (U_{v,1} − 𝔠'_v): e(U^{I'})H^0(X^{I',G_1}_1, ω^2(−D))_{m̃^{I',𝔠}} → e(U^I)H^0(X^{I,G_1}_1, ω^2(−D))_{m̃^{I,𝔠}} (7.9.3), which is the doubling theorem (Theorem 5.8.6 with Remark 5.8.7), owned with the higher Hida theory.

nodes.title: Theorem 7.9.4: Galois representations over the Hida–Hecke algebras
nodes.statement: Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1, with χ, I ⊆ S_p, 𝔠 and a (possibly empty) Taylor–Wiles datum Q. Extend the universal characters θ_v (v ∈ I) and θ_{v,1}, θ_{v,2} (v ∉ I) of §7.3 to G_{F_v} by Art_{F_v}(p) ↦ 1, and let λ_x be the unramified character with λ_x(Frob_v) = x. There is a unique deformation class, up to strict conjugacy, represented by a continuous ρ^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}: G_F → GSp_4(T^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}) which is a deformation of ρ̄ of type S_{χ,Q}^{I,𝔠}, such that R_{S_{χ,Q}^{I,𝔠}} → T^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} is a map of Λ_I[Δ_Q]-algebras, and: (1) for v ∉ S_p ∪ R ∪ {v_0} ∪ Q, det(X − ρ(Frob_v)) = Q_v(X); (2) for v ∈ I, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is conjugate to an upper triangular representation with diagonal (λ_{α̃_v}θ_v, λ_{β̃_v}θ_v, λ_{β̃_v}^{−1}θ_v^{−1}ε^{−1}, λ_{α̃_v}^{−1}θ_v^{−1}ε^{−1}) and vanishing (1,2) and (3,4) entries; (3) for v ∈ I^c, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is conjugate to an upper triangular representation with diagonal (λ_{U_{v,1}}θ_{v,1}, λ_{U_{v,2}/U_{v,1}}θ_{v,2}, λ_{U_{v,2}/U_{v,1}}^{−1}θ_{v,2}^{−1}ε^{−1}, λ_{U_{v,1}}^{−1}θ_{v,1}^{−1}ε^{−1}).
hypotheses: Hypothesis 7.8.1.
proofSteps: Case I = ∅: M^{χ,∅,𝔠,Q} is finite free over Λ_∅ (Proposition 7.8.11), so it injects, T̃^{∅,Q}-equivariantly, into the product of its specializations M ⊗_{Λ_∅,κ} E over the classical weights with k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 4 and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 or p+1 mod 2(p−1), which are scheme-theoretically dense in Spec Λ_∅. At such weights Lemma 7.8.5, the classicality Theorem 6.6.5 and Theorem 3.10.1 identify the specializations with ordinary cuspidal forms of regular weight, whose Galois representations (Theorem 2.7.2, with Propositions 2.4.13, 2.4.26, 2.4.28, 2.4.30 and Remark 2.4.31 for the local shapes) satisfy (1)–(3).

Glue these representations into a GSp_4(T)-valued representation as in Clozel–Harris–Taylor Proposition 3.4.4 (with Gee–Geraghty Lemma 7.1.1), using residual absolute irreducibility to pass from determinants to a representation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1); check the type at v ∈ Q with Lemma 7.4.4.

For general I, use doubling surjections and both choices of the ordinary unit root at each newly added v. Chebotarev and residual absolute irreducibility identify the resulting global deformation classes. The two ordinary flags then split the rank-two unramified block, forcing both (1,2) and (3,4) entries to vanish. A single stabilization gives an ordinary flag but does not by itself establish the Klingen splitting.

nodes.title: Corollary 7.9.6: refined Galois representations of ordinary weight 2 forms
nodes.statement: Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2, central character |·|^2, ordinary at every v | p, with p > 2 splitting completely in F. Then ρ_{π,p} of Theorem 1.8.17 (BCGP25) satisfies: (1) for finite v ∤ p with π_v unramified, ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified with det(X − ρ_{π,p}(Frob_v)) = Q_v(X). If moreover ρ̄_{π,p} is vast and tidy, ρ̄_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary and the ordinary Hecke parameters satisfy ᾱ_v ≠ β̄_v for every v | p, then ρ_{π,p} is GSp_4-valued with (2) ν∘ρ_{π,p} = ε^{−1}; (3) WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2})^{ss} for finite v ∤ p; (4) for v | p, ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is conjugate to an upper triangular representation with diagonal (λ_{α_v}, λ_{β_v}, λ_{β_v}^{−1}ε^{−1}, λ_{α_v}^{−1}ε^{−1}) and vanishing (1,2) and (3,4) entries. The residual ordinarity hypothesis is added to the printed statement: its proof needs it to apply Theorem 7.9.4.
hypotheses: p > 2 splits completely in the totally real field F; π as stated.
For (2)–(4): ρ̄_{π,p} vast and tidy, p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary at every v | p, and ᾱ_v ≠ β̄_v.
proofSteps: If π is not of general type, ρ_{π,p} is reducible and (1) follows from the GL_1 and GL_2 cases (Lemma 2.9.1); (2)–(4) are vacuous because a reducible ρ̄ is not vast.
If π is of general type, Mok's Theorem 4.14 gives (1) and (3) with GL_4 values.

Choose a solvable totally real F'/F, linearly disjoint from the fixed field of ker ρ̄_{π,p}, in which p splits completely, which trivializes ρ̄ at the places above the ramification of π and makes q_w ≡ 1 mod p (mod 9 if p = 3) there, and over which the base change of π has Iwahori-fixed vectors everywhere (Mok, Proposition 4.13). This repairs the printed proof, which arranges only the last two properties: Hypothesis 7.8.1(4)(a) and (5)(c) need the first two.

Hypothesis 7.8.1 then holds over F' (its clause (3) is the added residual ordinarity), and Theorem 7.9.4 with I = S_p, χ = 1, Q = ∅ gives the GSp_4-valued representation with the shape (4) over F'; (4) over F follows since p splits in F' and the local representations at v | p are unchanged. Compare with Theorem 1.8.17, which gives the same ρ_{π,p} without the residual hypotheses.

nodes.title: Proposition 7.9.8: Δ_Q-coinvariants of the Taylor–Wiles modules
nodes.statement: Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1, with χ, I, 𝔠 and a Taylor–Wiles datum Q. The natural map M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} → M^{χ,I,𝔠} induces an isomorphism (M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q})_{Δ_Q} ≅ M^{χ,I,𝔠}.

proofSteps: Use coherent descent and the Hecke relations to compare the Taylor–Wiles and original Hida complexes after forgetting the Taylor–Wiles factors and applying the partial localizations in (7.9.9)–(7.9.10). These comparisons hold in all degrees. The final selection of the anaemic maximal ideal uses uniqueness in the support only after RHom^0, equivalently in the relevant H^0 of specialized forms; do not assert a fully localized all-degree comparison.

nodes.title: Hypothesis 7.13.1 on ρ and the levels K^{p,Iw}, K^{p,Iw_1}
nodes.statement: A continuous ρ: G_F → GSp_4(O) satisfies Hypothesis 7.13.1 if: (1) F is totally real and p ≥ 3 splits completely in F; (2) ν∘ρ = ε^{−1}; (3) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is pure for every finite v; (4) for v ∈ S_p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary with unit eigenvalues α_v, β_v ∈ E; (5) there is a finite set R of places prime to p with ρ unramified outside R ∪ S_p and, for v ∈ R, q_v ≡ 1 mod p (mod 9 if p = 3), ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial and ρ|_{G_{F_v}} with only unipotent ramification; (6) there is an ordinary cuspidal π of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄, π_v unramified for v ∉ R ∪ S_p, π_v^{Iw(v)} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R ∪ S_p, and ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} pure for all finite v; (7) ρ̄ is vast and tidy. Then Hypothesis 7.8.1 holds for ρ̄ (Remark 7.13.2), and one fixes an absolutely unramified v_0 ∉ S_p ∪ R with q_{v_0} ≢ 1 mod p, residue characteristic > 5, ρ unramified at v_0 and no ratio of eigenvalues of ρ(Frob_{v_0}) congruent to q_{v_0} mod λ. The levels are K^{p,Iw} = ∏K_v and K^{p,Iw_1} = ∏K'_v with K_v = Iw(v), K'_v = Iw_1(v) for v ∈ R, K_{v_0} = K'_{v_0} = Iw_1(v_0), and hyperspecial elsewhere (Definition 7.13.4).

nodes.title: Proposition 7.13.5: Iwahori invariants of generic L-packets on components of Spec R_v^1
nodes.statement: Let v ∈ R and η_v a generic point of Spec R_v^1, the Ihara-avoidance ring of §7.4.5 with χ = 1. The rank n(η_v) of the monodromy operator is generically constant on the component Spec R_v^{1,η_v}; the set of y ∈ Spec R_v^{1,η_v}(Ē) whose L-packet L(ρ_y) contains a generic representation is nonempty; and d_{η_v} := Σ_{π∈L(ρ_y)} dim π^{Iw(v)} is independent of such y, with d_{η_v} = 8, 4, 4, 1 for n(η_v) = 0, 1, 2, 3. For η = (η_v)_{v∈R}, d_η := ∏_v d_{η_v}; for ρ as in Hypothesis 7.13.1, d_ρ := d_η for the unique generic point carrying the ρ|_{G_{F_v}} (unique by purity), so d_ρ = 8^{|R_0|}4^{|R_1|+|R_2|} with R_i = {v ∈ R : n(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}) = i}.
hypotheses: v ∈ R, so ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is trivial and q_v ≡ 1 mod p.
proofSteps: The components of Spec R_v^1 and their monodromy ranks are Proposition 7.4.7 and §§7.4.9–7.4.21, owned by LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2.

The generic L-packets with unipotent parameters are, by Roberts–Schmidt Tables A.1, A.7, A.15 and §1 of their newform paper (owned by the GSp_4 Part II of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions): type I (n = 0), IIa (n = 1), IIIa or {VIa, VIb} (n = 2), IVa (n = 3); type Va does not occur since it never corresponds to a residually trivial representation.
Read off dim π^{Iw(v)} from the tables (8, 4, 4 and 1 respectively, the pair {VIa, VIb} contributing 3 + 1).

nodes.title: Proposition 7.13.9: the doubling injection from Klingen to Iwahori level
nodes.statement: Let ρ = ρ_x satisfy Hypothesis 7.13.1. For I ⊆ S_p, w ∈ I^c, K^p as in Definition 7.13.4 and a choice 𝔠, the map (U_{w,1} − 𝔠'_w): S^{I∪{w},𝔠}_{κ_2,K^pK_p(I∪{w})}[𝔭̃_x^{I∪{w},𝔠}] → S^{I,𝔠}_{κ_2,K^pK_p(I)}[𝔭̃_x^{I,𝔠}] is injective, where 𝔠'_w is the unit eigenvalue of ρ_x at w not reducing to 𝔠_w.

Reduce to O-coefficients and then to the injectivity of (7.9.3) at w, proved in Proposition 7.9.1 from the doubling theorem (Theorem 5.8.6, owned with the higher Hida theory).

nodes.title: Proposition 7.13.11: dimensions of eigenspaces in regular weight and in weight κ_2
nodes.statement: In the setting of the proof of Theorem 7.13.6, let ρ_reg be a point of weight κ_reg in the support of M^{1,∅,𝔠}/𝔭_{κ_reg} on the same component of R_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} as ρ, ρ^χ_reg a point of weight κ_reg in the support of M^{χ,∅,𝔠}/𝔭_{κ_reg}, and π the representation of Hypothesis 7.13.1(6). Then dim_E S^{∅,𝔠}_{κ_reg,K^{p,Iw}K_p(∅)}[𝔭̃^{∅,𝔠}_{x_reg}] = 8d_ρ, dim_E S^{∅,𝔠}_{κ_reg,K^{p,Iw_1}K_p(∅),χ}[𝔭̃^{∅,𝔠}_{x^χ_reg}] = 8 and dim_E S^{I,𝔠}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[𝔭̃^{I,𝔠}_π] ≥ 8d_{ρ_{π,p}} (7.13.10); moreover there are automorphic π_reg, π^χ_reg of weight κ_reg and central character |·|^2 with ρ_{π_reg,p} ≅ ρ_reg and ρ_{π^χ_reg,p} ≅ ρ^χ_reg.
hypotheses: Hypothesis 7.13.1; Arthur's classification for GSp_4 in the conditional form carried by ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4.
proofSteps: By Theorems 6.6.5 and 3.10.1 the first space has dimension Σ_π dim (π^∞)^{K^{p,Iw}K_p(∅)} on the U-eigenspace, over cuspidal π of weight κ_reg, central character |·|^2, holomorphic at infinity, with ρ_{π,p} ≅ ρ_reg.

Such π are of general type (Lemma 2.9.1); strong multiplicity one for GL_4 (Jacquet–Shalika) and Theorem 2.9.3 rewrite the sum as (Σ_{π_{v_0}∈L(ρ_reg|_{G_{F_{v_0}}})} dim π_{v_0}^{Iw_1(v_0)})·∏_{v∈R}(Σ_{π_v∈L(ρ_reg|_{G_{F_v}})} dim π_v^{Iw(v)}).

Hyperspecial invariants are one-dimensional; at v ∈ S_p the ordinary contribution is one-dimensional (Propositions 2.4.24, 2.4.26); dim π_{v_0}^{Iw_1(v_0)} = 8 (Propositions 2.4.6, 2.4.3, 2.4.4 and the choice of v_0); at v ∈ R apply Proposition 7.13.5, using purity (Theorem 2.7.2(4)), genericity of the Weil–Deligne representation (Lemma 7.1.3) and Proposition 2.4.22.
For ρ^χ_reg each v ∈ R contributes 1 by Proposition 2.4.28; for π, (7.13.10) is its own contribution, which occurs by Theorem 3.10.1.

nodes.statement: Assume Hypothesis 7.13.1 for ρ = ρ_x. For every I ⊆ S_p with #I ≤ 1 and every choice 𝔠, dim_E S^{I,𝔠}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[𝔭̃_x^{I,𝔠}] = 8d_ρ. The factor 8 = |W| comes from the level Iw_1(v_0) at the auxiliary place, where no Hecke condition is imposed (Remark 7.13.7).
hypotheses: Hypothesis 7.13.1.
proofSteps: Case I = ∅: M_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} is maximal Cohen–Macaulay (Proposition 7.11.2), so the cycle comparison of Lemmas 7.12.2–7.12.3 (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9, with cycles at R03.6) applies to M_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} and M_∞^{χ,∅,𝔠}. Since Spec (R_v^χ)' is irreducible for χ_{v,1}, χ_{v,2} ≠ 1 and χ_{v,1} ≠ χ_{v,2}^{±1} (Proposition 7.4.8), Spec (R_∞^χ)' is irreducible and the nonzero maximal Cohen–Macaulay M_∞^{χ,∅,𝔠} is supported on all of it; comparing the cycles of M_∞^1/λ ≅ M_∞^χ/λ then shows that M_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} is supported on every component of Spec (R_∞^1)'.

For the integral cycle comparison, import Propositions 7.4.17(1) and 7.4.21: every nonzero coefficient of the relevant special-fibre component cycles is one, and the specialized component cycles have the required incidence relations. This is needed to recover integer multiplicities, not merely equality of rational supports. Nonvanishing of the χ-patched module follows from its mod-λ identification with the nonzero 1-module and Nakayama.

M_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} is finite free over S_∞ and faithful over (R_∞^{1,∅,𝔠})^{red}, so Spec R_∞ → Spec S_∞ is surjective and generalizing; this produces regular-weight points x_reg on the component of x and x^χ_reg.

Proposition 7.13.11 gives the dimensions 8d_ρ and 8 at these points; Lemma 7.13.8 (generic rank on smooth points, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3) applies at smooth points (purity, Theorem 2.7.2, Lemmas 7.1.3 and 7.3.18) and transports 8d_ρ to x, giving d'_η = d_ρ with Lemma 7.12.3.

Case #I = 1: the same argument at the component of π gives d'_{η_π} = d_{ρ_{π,p}}; with (7.13.10) and Lemmas 7.12.3 and 7.13.8 it gives dim ≥ 8d_ρ, and the doubling injection (Proposition 7.13.9) bounds the dimension by that of the I = ∅ space, 8d_ρ.

acceptance: For I = ∅ and every choice 𝔠 the four spaces of §8.1 (two places) all have dimension 8d_ρ.
In particular the eigenspace is nonzero, so ρ is the Galois representation of a p-adic ordinary weight 2 form at every level I with #I ≤ 1.

nodes.title: Lemmas 8.2.3 and 8.2.5: analytic continuation and étale descent of the glued forms
nodes.statement: Setting: the inductive step of Theorem 8.2.1, with #I ≥ 2, I = J ⊔ {v_1, v_2}, the choice 𝔠 fixed on J ∪ I^c, and the 8d_ρ-dimensional overconvergent eigenspaces V_{𝔠_1,𝔠_2} (Iwahori level at v_1, v_2), V_{α_1+β_1,𝔠_2} (Klingen at v_1) and V_{𝔠_1,α_2+β_2} (Klingen at v_2) given by the inductive hypothesis. For (ε_v) let 𝒳((ε_v)) be the open where deg H_v ≥ 1 − ε_v (v ∈ I, H_v the order-p subgroup of the Klingen structure) and deg L_v ≥ 2 − ε_v (v ∈ I^c, L_v the rank-p^2 isotropic subgroup of the Iwahori structure), with Fargues' degree; 𝒳^{mult,†} = lim_{ε→0+}𝒳((ε_v)), 𝒳^{mult,‡} the same limit over places other than v_1, v_2, and 𝒴 ⊂ 𝒳 the good reduction loci. Lemma 8.2.3: elements of V_{𝔠_1,𝔠_2} extend to 𝒳^{mult,‡, d^H_1 ≥ 1−ε, d^H_2 ≥ 1−ε, d^L_1 > 1, d^L_2 > 1}_{Iw(v_1,v_2)} for some ε > 0, and the Klingen-level spaces extend to the analogous regions with Iwahori level only at the other place. Lemma 8.2.5: on U_ε = 𝒴^{mult,‡, d^H_1 ≥ 1−ε, d^H_2 ≥ 1−ε, d^L_2 > 1}_{Iw(v_1,v_2)} the forgetful map q_{v_2} is étale onto 𝒴^{mult,‡, d^H_1 ≥ 1−ε, d^H_2 ≥ 1−ε}_{Iw(v_1)} and surjective for small ε; after shrinking ε every element of V_{α_1,α_2+β_2} descends along q_{v_2}. With the isomorphism (U_{v_1,1} − β_1): V_{α_1+β_1,α_2} ⊕ V_{α_1+β_1,β_2} ≅ V_{α_1,α_2} ⊕ V_{α_1,β_2} (8.2.4), the preimage of V_{α_1,α_2+β_2} is an 8d_ρ-dimensional space of eigenforms of Klingen level at v_1 and v_2 descending to 𝒴^{mult,‡, d^H_1 ≥ 1−ε, d^H_2 ≥ 1−ε}.
hypotheses: The forms are ordinary, hence of finite slope for U_{w,1}.
proofSteps: Analytic continuation in the I^c-directions: restriction is an isomorphism on U_{w,1}-finite slope parts (Lemma 6.5.18, owned with the higher Coleman theory), and Kassaei-style continuation one form at a time.
(8.2.4) is an isomorphism because each map U_{v_1,1} − β_1 is injective (doubling injection, Proposition 7.13.9) between spaces of the same dimension 8d_ρ.

Étale descent along q_{v_2}: compare the two pullbacks on the fibre product; connected components of the shrinking neighbourhoods are controlled by Poineau's theorem (8.2.6) and by Lemmas 8.2.7–8.2.11; Koecher's principle extends across the boundary.

Complete the descent with the normalized trace G = deg(q_{v_2})^{−1} q_{v_2,*}F (arXiv pp. 242–243). Trace commutes with U_{v_1,1} at the other place; applying the doubling operator to F − q_{v_2}^*G gives zero, and its injectivity proves F = q_{v_2}^*G. This produces an actual descended section, beyond component control.

sources.match: Extends the eigenforms supplied by the induction to explicit neighbourhoods defined by degrees of the canonical subgroups, and descends the forms of Klingen level at one place along the étale forgetful map at the other, producing Klingen level at both.

acceptance: For #I = 2 and S_p = {v_1, v_2} this is the argument sketched in §8.1.
The descended space has the same dimension 8d_ρ as each of its inputs.

nodes.title: Lemmas 8.2.7–8.2.11: connected components and the superspecial locus
nodes.statement: (8.2.7) If S → T is a finite étale map of adic spaces of finite type over a field, the image of a connected component of S is a connected component of T. (8.2.8) Every connected component of the mod p locus Y^{I,=_{v_2}1}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I),1} (p-rank 1 at v_2) contains a point of Y^{I,=_{{v_1,v_2}}1}, and every connected component of Y^{I,=_{v_2}2} contains a point of Y^{I,=_{v_1}1,=_{v_2}2}; here I means H_v multiplicative for v ∈ I and the canonical ordinary Iwahori structure on I^c. (8.2.9) Every connected component of 𝒴^{mult,‡, d^H_1 = d^H_2 = 1, =_{v_2}1}_{Iw(v_1)} or 𝒴^{mult,‡, d^H_1 = d^H_2 = 1, =_{v_2}2}_{Iw(v_1)} contains a point non-ordinary at v_1. (8.2.10) For J ⊆ S_p and hyperspecial level at p, each irreducible component of Y^{=_{J^c}2,=_J1}_1 contains a superspecial point (p-rank 0 at every place) in its closure. (8.2.11) At Iwahori level, for J ⊆ J' ⊆ S_p, every irreducible component of the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratum Y^{=_{J^c}2,=_J1,m-can}_1 contains a point of Y^{=_{(J')^c}2,=_{J'}1,m-can}_1 in its closure.
hypotheses: Y_{…,1} denotes the special fibre of the open Hilbert–Siegel variety; the Ekedahl–Oort and Kottwitz–Rapoport stratifications are owned by the Hilbert–Siegel Part II of HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves.
proofSteps: (8.2.7): such spaces have finitely many connected components, and finite étale maps are open and closed (Huber, Lemma 1.4.5 and Proposition 1.7.8; AdicSpacesPartII R2–R3).

(8.2.10): the Ekedahl–Oort stratification extends to the minimal compactification with affine open strata, and the superspecial locus does not meet the boundary; an affine stratum of positive dimension has a smaller stratum in its closure.

For Lemma 8.2.11, project a KR stratum to hyperspecial level via the proper map. Its closure meets a superspecial EO stratum by Lemma 8.2.10. Use the local-model closure order to find a p-rank-zero KR stratum in the appropriate two closures, then use the canonical section and density of the generic p-rank strata. The local-model incidence assertion is an explicit part of the Hilbert–Siegel H4 supplier contract; quasi-affineness at Iwahori level is not assumed (Remark 8.2.12).

(8.2.8): the canonical section s of the projection from Iwahori level (L_w = 𝒢_w[F]) identifies the KR strata with the p-rank strata at level K_p(I), and density of the generic p-rank strata (§4.1) finishes; (8.2.9) follows by taking tubes (connectedness of tubes of connected components of the special fibre).

sources.match: Proves that connected components of the relevant ordinary and p-rank-one loci, at Klingen and Iwahori level, meet the smaller strata, using the Ekedahl–Oort and Kottwitz–Rapoport stratifications and Huber's results on finite étale maps.

acceptance: Over a single place (F = Q) the statements reduce to closure relations of the p-rank strata of the Siegel threefold.
They are used only to make the étale descent of Lemma 8.2.5 land on every connected component.

nodes.title: Theorem 8.2.1: the ρ-eigenspace has dimension 8d_ρ for every I
nodes.statement: Assume ρ satisfies Hypothesis 7.13.1. For every I ⊆ S_p and every choice 𝔠, dim_E S^{I,𝔠}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[𝔭̃_x^{I,𝔠}] = dim_{C_p} S^{I,𝔠,†}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[𝔭̃_x^{I,𝔠}] = 8d_ρ, where S^{I,𝔠,†} = e(U^I)H^0(𝒳^{G_1,mult,†}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}, ω^2(−D)) ∩ (S^{I,𝔠}_{κ_2} ⊗_E C_p), the intersection taken inside e(U^I)H^0(𝒳^{G_1,I}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}, ω^2(−D)) via the injective restriction from the dagger space.
hypotheses: Hypothesis 7.13.1.
proofSteps: Induction on #I. For #I ≤ 1: Theorem 7.13.6 and Theorem 6.6.4 (for #I ≤ 1 the ordinary overconvergent complex is the specialized Hida complex, so ordinary classes are overconvergent).
Upper bound for every I: restriction from S^{I,𝔠,†} is injective, and repeated doubling injections (Proposition 7.13.9) bound dim S^{I,𝔠}_{κ_2}[𝔭̃] by the I = ∅ dimension 8d_ρ.

Lower bound for #I ≥ 2: write I = J ⊔ {v_1, v_2}; the inductive hypothesis for J, J ∪ {v_1}, J ∪ {v_2} supplies the spaces V_{·,·}; Lemmas 8.2.3 and 8.2.5 produce an 8d_ρ-dimensional space of overconvergent eigenforms of Klingen level at v_1 and v_2.

sources.match: Extends the multiplicity theorem from #I ≤ 1 to all I by induction on #I, the upper bound coming from doubling and the lower bound from analytic continuation and étale descent.

acceptance: For I = S_p the theorem gives a nonzero space of ordinary overconvergent Klingen-level forms at every place above p, which Theorem 6.5.8 makes classical.
The dimension 8d_ρ does not depend on I.

nodes.title: Corollary 8.2.2: a representation satisfying Hypothesis 7.13.1 is modular
nodes.statement: Suppose ρ satisfies Hypothesis 7.13.1. Then ρ is modular: there is an ordinary cuspidal automorphic π' of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ and WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π'_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) for every finite v.
hypotheses: Hypothesis 7.13.1.
proofSteps: Theorem 8.2.1 with I = S_p gives nonzero overconvergent ordinary forms; the classicality Theorem 6.5.8 makes them classical and Theorem 3.10.1 identifies them with a cuspidal π' with ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ.

Corollary 7.9.6 (and Theorem 1.8.17) gives the semisimplified compatibility at every finite v. At v | p the full compatibility follows from Corollary 7.9.6(4), Proposition 2.4.24 and Lemma 2.5.1 with purity (the printed proof treats only R); at v ∉ R ∪ S_p both sides are unramified; the monodromy at v ∈ R remains.

Since ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is pure, by the corrected Lemma 2.5.1 (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.5: for dim 4 and symplectic N, maximal rank of N characterizes the pure structure) it suffices to show n(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}) ≤ n(π'_v). Roberts–Schmidt Table A.15 relates n(π_v) to vanishing of hyperspecial, paramodular, Klingen and Siegel parahoric invariants; if, say, n(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}) = 1 but π'_v had hyperspecial vectors, ρ would be a p-adic limit of regular-weight ρ_{π'',p} with n = 0 (Theorem 7.9.4 and Theorem 2.7.2), contradicting semicontinuity of the rank of N; the cases n = 2, 3 are the same.

sources.match: Deduces from the gluing theorem at I = S_p, classicality and the automorphic description that ρ is the Galois representation of a cuspidal weight 2 form, and matches monodromy at the Ihara-avoidance places through purity and the parahoric-vector table.

acceptance: The form π' has Iwahori-fixed vectors at the places of R and is unramified away from R ∪ S_p ∪ {v_0}.
The full Frobenius-semisimple compatibility holds at every finite place, as Definition 9.1.8 requires.

nodes.title: Lemma 8.3.2: solvable descent of modularity
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 split completely in the totally real F and F'/F be a solvable extension of totally real fields. Suppose ρ: G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) has (1) ν∘ρ = ε^{−1}; (2) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for v | p; (3) ρ̄ vast and tidy; (4) ρ|_{G_{F'}} irreducible and modular through an ordinary π' of GSp_4(A_{F'}) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with full Weil–Deligne compatibility at every finite place of F'. Then ρ is modular through an ordinary π of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, with WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) for every finite v. The same holds, with the same proof, when the central characters are |·|^2 times a finite order character, which Theorem 8.5.2 needs.
hypotheses: p > 2 totally split in F; F'/F solvable, F' totally real.
proofSteps: Reduce to F'/F cyclic of prime degree. ρ|_{G_{F'}} irreducible forces π' to be of general type, with cuspidal transfer Π' to GL_4(A_{F'}); cyclic descent (Arthur–Clozel, Chapter 3, Theorem 4.2) gives Π on GL_4(A_F) with BC_{F'/F}(Π) = Π'.

L^S(s, Π', ∧^2 ⊗ |·|^{−2}) = ∏_ψ L^S(s, Π, ∧^2 ⊗ |·|^{−2}ψ^{−1}) over characters ψ of A_F^×/F^×N(A_{F'}^×); the left side has a simple pole at s = 1, and by Shahidi all but at most one factor on the right are holomorphic and nonvanishing there, so one factor has a pole and Theorem 2.9.3 makes Π the transfer of a cuspidal π of GSp_4(A_F) of central character |·|^2ψ and parallel weight 2.

ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F'}} ≅ ρ|_{G_{F'}}, so ρ_{π,p} and ρ differ by a character of Gal(F'/F); twist π to make them GL_4-isomorphic; Lemma 8.3.1 (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7), using that the ratio of the two multipliers is trivial on G_{F′} and that ρ|_{G_{F′}} is irreducible; irreducibility over F alone does not imply uniqueness of a multiplier gives ν∘ρ_{π,p} = ε^{−1}, so π has central character |·|^2 and ρ_{π,p} ≅ ρ.
Corollary 7.9.6 gives the semisimplified compatibility; the monodromy is checked after base change, where it holds by (4).

sources.locator: Lemma 8.3.1, Lemma 8.3.2 and its proof, §8.3, pp. 246–247
sources.match: Proves that modularity descends along solvable extensions of totally real fields for representations with irreducible restriction, by cyclic descent for GL_4, Shahidi's nonvanishing of exterior square L-functions and Arthur's classification.

acceptance: It is the GSp_4 analogue of Lemma 1.3 of Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor.
For F' = F it is the identity.

nodes.title: Theorem 8.4.1: the main modularity lifting theorem
nodes.statement: Suppose p ≥ 3 splits completely in the totally real F and ρ: G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) satisfies: (0) ρ is unramified outside a finite set of places; (1) ν∘ρ = ε^{−1}; (2) ρ̄ is vast and tidy; (3) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for every v | p; (4) there is a cuspidal π of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, ordinary at every v | p, with ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄; (5) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} and ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} are pure for every finite v. Then ρ is modular: there is an ordinary π' of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ and WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π'_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) for every finite v. Hypothesis (0) is not printed but the proof uses it; every application has ρ from an abelian surface or a compatible system, which satisfies it.
hypotheses: p ≥ 3 totally split in F; (0)–(5) as stated.
proofSteps: Choose a solvable totally real F'/F, linearly disjoint from the fixed field of ker ρ̄, in which p splits completely, such that at every place w above a v ∤ p where π_v or ρ is ramified, ρ̄|_{G_{F'_w}} is trivial, ρ|_{G_{F'_w}} has only unipotent ramification and q_w ≡ 1 mod p^2, and over which π has a base change π' with Iwahori-fixed vectors at every finite place (Mok, Proposition 4.13). The auxiliary-extension construction is owned by PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.5; (0) makes the set of ramified places finite, so finitely many local conditions are imposed.
Then ρ|_{G_{F'}} satisfies Hypothesis 7.13.1 (vast and tidy is preserved by linear disjointness), so it is modular by Corollary 8.2.2.
ρ|_{G_{F'}} is irreducible since ρ̄|_{G_{F'}} is, and Lemma 8.3.2 descends modularity to F.

sources.match: States the main modularity lifting theorem for GSp_4-valued representations with inverse cyclotomic multiplier, vast and tidy residual image, p-distinguished weight 2 ordinarity at p and an ordinary residually modular seed, and proves it by solvable base change to Hypothesis 7.13.1 and descent.

acceptance: Every potential modularity and modularity result of §§9–10 is deduced from it.
Applied to ρ_{A,p} of an abelian surface it gives Proposition 10.1.1.

nodes.title: Twisted p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary representations and twisted ordinary π_p
nodes.statement: A representation ρ: G_{Q_p} → GSp_4(Q̄_p) is twisted p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary if it is an unramified twist ρ_0 ⊗ μ (μ an unramified character) of a representation ρ_0 that is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary (Definition 7.3.1). An admissible representation π_p of GSp_4(Q_p) is twisted ordinary if it is an unramified twist π_0 ⊗ (μ∘ν) of an ordinary π_0.
hypotheses: p ≥ 3; Definition 7.3.1 and the ordinary representations of GSp_4(Q_p) are owned by LocalGaloisDeformationRings and the GSp_4 Part II.
proofSteps: Unfold; the multiplier of ρ_0 ⊗ μ is ν(ρ_0)μ^2, so a twisted ordinary ρ has multiplier ε^{−1} times the square of an unramified character.

sources.match: Defines the twisted notions as unramified twists of p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary representations and of ordinary representations.

acceptance: Every p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary ρ is twisted with μ = 1.
Twisting does not change ρ̄|_{I_{Q_p}} up to an unramified character.

nodes.title: Theorem 8.5.2: modularity lifting with relaxed multiplier
nodes.statement: Suppose p ≥ 3 splits completely in the totally real F and ρ: G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) satisfies: (0) ρ is unramified outside a finite set; (1) ν∘ρ = χε^{−1}, χ totally even of finite order and unramified above p; (2) ρ̄ vast and tidy; (3) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} twisted p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for v | p; (4) there is π of parallel weight 2, twisted ordinary at every v | p, with ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄ (no condition on its central character); (5) ρ|_{G_{F_v}}, ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} pure for all finite v. Then there is a twisted ordinary π' of parallel weight 2 with ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ and WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π'_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) for every finite v.
hypotheses: The paper sketches the proof and does not use the theorem elsewhere; this plan writes the sketch out.
proofSteps: Write ν∘ρ_π = χ′ε^{−1}. Residual isomorphism gives χ̄′ = χ̄, not χ′ = χ. Since χ is totally even and p > 2, so is χ′. Choose a quadratic totally real F′/F disjoint from the field cut out by ρ̄, with p fully split, and finite-order roots ψ² = χ|_{G_{F′}}, (ψ′)² = χ′|_{G_{F′}}, unramified at p, with ψ̄ = ψ̄′. The Brauer obstruction and prescribed local roots are imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2/R02.4; adjust quadratic choices to match reductions. Simultaneous roots with these local and disjointness constraints, not just an abstract square root, are the required contract.

Apply Theorem 8.4.1 to ρ|_{G_{F'}} ⊗ ψ^{−1} and π_{F'} ⊗ (ψ')^{−1}∘Art_{F'}; it gives modularity of ρ|_{G_{F'}} ⊗ ψ^{−1}, hence of ρ|_{G_{F'}} after twisting back (the paper prints ⊗ψ here; ⊗ψ^{−1} is meant).
Descend with Lemma 8.3.2 in its general-central-character form: the same proof with central character |·|^2 replaced by |·|^2 times a finite order character, Lemma 8.3.1 now fixing ν∘ρ = χε^{−1}.

nodes.title: Galois types of abelian surfaces and challenging surfaces
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian surface over a totally real F and L/F the minimal (Galois) extension over which all endomorphisms of A are defined. The Galois type of A/F is the Gal(L/F)-module End_L(A) ⊗_Z R (Fité–Kedlaya–Rotger–Sutherland); the types fall into six families A–F. Independently of l, the representations ρ_{A,l} fall into exactly one of: (1) strongly irreducible (type A); (2) reducible (types B[C_1], C, E[C_n], some D, some F); (3) potentially abelian but not reducible (the remaining D and F); (4) induced from a quadratic K/F but not potentially abelian, with the two 2-dimensional constituents over K either (a) equivalent up to twist (type E[D_n]) or (b) not (type B[C_2]). A/F is challenging if it has type A (equivalently End_C A = Z) or B[C_2]. In type B[C_2] there are a quadratic K/F (Gal(K/F) = {1,σ}) and a strongly irreducible weakly compatible system 𝒮 = (s_l) of rank 2, weight 0 representations of G_K with determinant ε_l^{−1} such that 𝓡_A ≅ Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}𝒮, and s_l^σ, s_l never become isomorphic over a finite extension of K.
hypotheses: F totally real; A an abelian surface over F; 𝓡_A as in AP.0.

nodes.title: Proposition 9.2.1: surfaces not of type A or B[C_2] are potentially automorphic
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian surface over a totally real F not of type A or B[C_2]. Then A is potentially automorphic.
hypotheses: F totally real.
proofSteps: For types D and F, pass to a finite extension L over which all CM endomorphisms are defined. Then the system is abelian and automorphic through Hecke characters (CM.4). Such L need not be totally real; obtaining analytic statements back over F uses the CM/Brauer argument, not a claim that all CM endomorphisms are defined over a totally real extension.

Types B[C_1], C and E other than E[D_n]: 𝓡_A = 𝓡^1 ⊕ 𝓡^2 with irreducible odd weight 0 rank 2 systems over F, each potentially automorphic by Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor Theorem 5.4.1 (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2).

Type E[D_n]: 𝓡_A ≅ Ind_{G_{F'}}^{G_F}𝒮 with s_l^σ ≅ s_l ⊗ δ_l for a finite order δ. For a density one set of l (Lemma 9.1.10(2), PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5; BLGGT Prop. 5.3.2) fix l > 7 with Sym^2 s̄_l|_{G_{F'(ζ_l)}} irreducible, l unramified in F', s_l, ε_l crystalline above l. Proj s_l extends to G_F → PGL_2(Q̄_l) and lifts (Tate's H^2(G_F, Q/Z) = 0, ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4; Patrikis Lemmas 2.3.17, 2.7.4, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7) to r̃: G_F → GL_2(Q̄_l), Hodge–Tate of weights (0,1), with r̃|_{G_{F'}} = s_l ⊗ ψ; after a twist r̃ is crystalline above l, odd (Calegari–Gee Prop. 2.5), hence potentially automorphic (BLGGT Thm. 4.5.1), and ρ_{A,l} ≅ Ind(r̃|_{G_{F'}} ⊗ ψ^{−1}).

nodes.title: Lemma 9.2.2: big residual image for challenging surfaces
nodes.statement: If A/F is a challenging abelian surface, then ρ̄_{A,l} is vast and tidy for a set of primes l of Dirichlet density one. In type A this follows from Serre's theorem that ρ̄_{A,l}(G_F) = GSp_4(F_l) for all large l, with Lemma 7.5.15. In type B[C_2], ρ_{A,l} = Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}s_l and Lemma 7.5.22 applies, except for the case to be treated separately: A has real multiplication by a real quadratic M defined over K but not over F and l is inert in M; then the two projective constituents can be related by the nontrivial field automorphism τ. The corrected semilinear-image argument of extraction E109 is required; neither a specified split semidirect product nor a centre of order at least three is asserted.
hypotheses: A challenging; F totally real.
proofSteps: Type A: Serre's open image theorem for abelian surfaces with End_C = Z over a number field (owned by the OpenImage Part II of FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems); GSp_4(F_l) with surjective multiplier is vast and tidy (Lemma 7.5.15, G7).

Type B[C_2], general case: SL_2(O_M/λ) ⊂ s̄_λ(G_K) for almost all λ by Ribet's large image theorem for abelian varieties with real multiplication (no potential inner twists since s_l, s_l^σ never become isomorphic), owned by the same Part II; then Lemma 7.5.22.

In the field-twisted case, use the corrected G7 contract from extraction E109: the image over F(ζ_l) has an index-two subgroup N = {(A, ±τ(A)) : A ∈ SL_2(k)}, with τ the nontrivial field involution of k; no splitting of the index-two extension is assumed. Prove enormousness using nonisomorphism of V and V^τ, the requisite H^1 vanishings on Sym²V and V⊗V^τ, and the coset element built from C ∈ SL_2(k^τ) of order #k^τ+1 (Lemmas 7.5.14, 7.5.17). For tidiness use an element of the full similitude image with multiplier −1 and eigenvalues a, −a^{−1}, ±τ(a), ∓τ(a)^{−1}, chosen to avoid eigenvalue ratio −1. The centre of SL_2(k) has order two, so the old centre argument fails.

Lemma 7.5.22 as printed uses Aut(PSL_2(k)) = PGL_2(k), which is false (it is PΓL_2(k)); it must be applied with k = F_l, or with the Frobenius-twisted case separated as above (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7).

nodes.title: Lemmas 9.2.5–9.2.6: good primes have density one, and the auxiliary pair p, q
nodes.statement: Let A/F be a challenging abelian surface. (9.2.5) The good primes for A have relative density one among the primes splitting completely in F. (9.2.6) There are distinct good primes p, q such that ρ̄_{A,q}(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues for every v | p. For Lemma 9.2.7, p is fixed first and q is then chosen with q > p^2 and Frob_q conjugate to complex conjugation in the Galois closure over Q of F(A[p], ζ_p, √Δ_v : v | p), Δ_v = a_1(v)^2 − 4a_2(v) + 8p; this is a positive-density Chebotarev condition on primes split in F, and it forces q ≡ −1 mod p and every Δ_v to be a square mod q.
hypotheses: A challenging; a_1(v), a_2(v) the Frobenius coefficients at v | p for a good prime p.
proofSteps: 9.2.5 (after Sawin and Calegari–Geraghty Lemma A.7): by Lemma 9.2.2 it suffices that ρ_{A,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for density one; at a place of good reduction above p with Frobenius polynomial x^4 − a_1x^3 + a_2x^2 − pa_1x + p^2, A is ordinary iff p ∤ a_2, and then the condition holds iff p ∤ a_1^2 − 4a_2 (Katz–Messing compares crystalline and l-adic Frobenius polynomials; requested at AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4).

By the Weil bounds p | a_1^2 − 4a_2 forces a_1^2 − 4a_2 = pc with c in a finite set; Chebotarev on the Zariski closure of ρ_{A,l}(G_F) reduces density one to non-constancy of the trace of (V^{⊗2} − 4∧^2V) ⊗ χ^{−1} on each component of the Sato–Tate group (USp_4 in type A, the normalizer of SU_2 × SU_2 in type B[C_2]); this density argument is owned by the OpenImage Part II.

9.2.6: at a good prime p the crystalline Frobenius eigenvalues on T_pA at v | p are distinct, so ρ̄_{A,q}(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues for all but finitely many q of good reduction; the strengthened choice of q is one more Chebotarev condition.

For the strengthened choice of q, Δ_v = a_1² − 4a_2 + 8p is the square of the difference of the two real Weil traces α+p/α and β+p/β. Distinct unit roots and ordinarity give Δ_v > 0. Thus all Q(√Δ_v) are real, and complex conjugation fixes them while acting by −1 on μ_p; this makes the simultaneous Chebotarev conditions compatible.

nodes.title: Twisted moduli of principally polarized abelian surfaces with fixed torsion
nodes.statement: Let F' be a number field, odd n ≥ 3 an integer (a prime, a product pq of distinct primes, or 3), and V a finite symplectic G_{F'}-module free of rank 4 over Z/n with multiplier ε̄^{−1}. Y(V)/F' is the moduli space of pairs (B, ı) of a principally polarized abelian surface B and a symplectic isomorphism ı: B[n] ≅ V^∨ (Weil pairing against the dual pairing). It is a smooth geometrically connected quasi-projective variety over F', a twist of the Siegel moduli space 𝒜_2(n) of full level n, to which it becomes isomorphic over F̄'. Its good ordinary local locus is open. A local point requires a principally polarized ordinary surface whose entire n-torsion realizes V^∨. At real places the odd-level anti-symplectic involution has two complementary rank-two eigenspaces, and polarized complex uniformization gives a real point. At a finite place the existence of only one primary part of the level is insufficient.
hypotheses: odd n ≥ 3, so the moduli problem is rigid and representable; the Weil pairing convention of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3.
proofSteps: Construct Y(V) as the twist of the fine moduli scheme 𝒜_2(n) (PELModuli M5–M6) by the Isom torsor between V^∨ and (Z/n)^4 with its standard form; geometric connectedness holds because the multiplier of V is ε̄^{−1}, matching the Weil pairing's target μ_n, so the Weil-pairing component is the one selected (compare the Hilbert analogue HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H6).

At v|p for n=pq, a given principally polarized ordinary A supplies a point only when both A[p] and A[q] match the prescribed dual modules. At v|q, start with a polarized ordinary special fibre; specify its finite-flat q-primary part and the prime-to-q level on its canonical lift, then check the prescribed generic-fibre n-torsion. Do not treat B_0[q] over characteristic q as a free rank-four étale Galois module. In the switch use V = ρ̄_{A,p} ⊕ ρ̄_q, so V^∨ = A[p] ⊕ ρ̄_q^∨.

nodes.title: Fixed-determinant GL_2(F_q)-extensions with prescribed local behaviour
nodes.statement: Let E'/E be finite extensions of number fields, F^{(avoid)}/E finite Galois, S a finite set of places of E, q a prime, ψ̄: G_E → F_q^× a character cut out inside F^{(avoid)} with ψ̄(G_{E'}) = F_q^×, and for v ∈ S local Galois extensions with GL_2(F_q)-valued local data of determinant ψ̄. Then there are a finite extension K/E, linearly disjoint from E'F^{(avoid)}/E and with the prescribed splitting at S, and, over K' = KE', a representation r̄: G_{K'} → GL_2(F_q) with det r̄ = ψ̄, image GL_2(F_q), L' ∩ K'F^{(avoid)} = K'(ψ̄) for the fixed field L' of ker r̄, and the prescribed local data at the places above S (the variant of Proposition 9.1.12 used by Lemma 9.2.7). No descent of L' to an extension of K is asserted.
hypotheses: E, E' number fields; S finite; the local data have determinant ψ̄.
proofSteps: Use a generically free open U in the regular linear representation of G=GL_2(F_q), with H=SL_2(F_q) and D=G/H. The finite D-cover U/H → U/G can be twisted by the determinant torsor ψ̄. The resulting parameter variety is geometrically irreducible, and pulling back U → U/G gives a G-torsor with the specified determinant. Versality of U gives local points realizing each prescribed local G-torsor over the infinite local fields. Apply Moret-Bailly to its Weil restriction from E′ to E, retaining the local conditions and avoidance extension.

Add to S auxiliary places of E split completely in E′F^{(avoid)}. With the determinant trivializations retained, prescribe unramified local data meeting every SL_2(F_q)-conjugacy class. The final restriction argument below forces image ⊇ SL_2(F_q), and det = ψ̄ with ψ̄(G_{E′}) = F_q^× gives image GL_2(F_q).
Keeping the asymmetric local choices at the two places above a split auxiliary place requires working over K' without descending L'.

Retain the determinant trivialization in the parameter problem, so local comparisons are by H=SL_2-conjugacy. Choose the auxiliary Frobenii to meet every H-conjugacy class at places split in E′F^{(avoid)}, and require those places to split in K. They are Frobenii in G_{K′F^{(avoid)}}. Jordan’s lemma applied to H therefore gives r̄(G_{K′F^{(avoid)}})=H, while det r̄=ψ̄ cuts out K′(ψ̄). This proves L′ ∩ K′F^{(avoid)}=K′(ψ̄); surjectivity merely over K′ would not suffice.

nodes.statement: Let A/F be a challenging abelian surface over a totally real field. Then A is potentially modular: there are a finite Galois extension of totally real fields F'/F and a prime p splitting completely in F' such that ρ_{A,p}|_{G_{F'}} is modular and irreducible.
hypotheses: F totally real; A challenging.
proofSteps: Resolve the polarization gap before applying the principally polarized Y(V) construction to arbitrary A. The hypotheses only give a prime-to-pq polarization. Either give a local principal-polarization replacement preserving the required torsion, or develop the analogous smooth geometrically connected twisted moduli for a fixed polarization type prime to pq, with both ordinary local points. No such replacement or general-type contract is established by this design.

Take p, q, F_1, F', r̄_q, ρ̄_q from Lemma 9.2.7. Let Y/F' be the twisted moduli space of (B, ı_p, ı_q) with ı_p: B[p] ≅ A[p]|_{G_{F'}} and ı_q: B[q] ≅ ρ̄_q^∨; it is smooth and geometrically connected, and Ω_v = Y^{ord}(F'_v) is nonempty for v | pq∞ (A at v | p; the canonical lift of E × E' with traces p, −p at v | q; real points from det r̄_q^∨ = ε).
Moret-Bailly (R23.1) gives a totally real F''/F', with p and q split, linearly disjoint from the relevant kernels, and B/F'' with good ordinary reduction above p and q.

Proposition 9.1.11 (R23.2, R23.3, R23.5) gives, after enlarging F'', a q-ordinary weight 0 form 𝛑 on GL_2(A_{F_1F''}) with trivial central character, unramified above pq, with ρ̄_{𝛑,q} ≅ r̄_q|_{G_{F_1F''}}; Roberts' theta lift (GSp_4 Part II) gives an ordinary π on GSp_4(A_{F''}) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 (printed: trivial) whose GL_4 transfer is the automorphic induction of 𝛑 ⊗ |·|, so ρ_{π,q} ≅ Ind ρ_{𝛑,q} lifts ρ̄_q|_{G_{F''}}; ρ_{π,q} is pure (Blasius away from q, Caraiani at q).

Theorem 8.4.1 at q makes ρ_{B,q} modular, hence ρ_{B,p}; Theorem 8.4.1 at p then makes ρ_{A,p}|_{G_{F''}} modular (purity of ρ_{B,q}, ρ_{B,p}, ρ_{A,p} from Proposition 2.8.1). Irreducibility comes from the vast residual image.

sources.match: Proves potential modularity of challenging abelian surfaces by a p–q switch: an auxiliary surface B shares A's p-torsion and has q-torsion induced from GL_2, which is potentially modular; the lifting theorem is applied twice.

acceptance: Every surface with End_C A = Z over a totally real field is potentially modular.
The extension F'' can be chosen linearly disjoint from any given finite extension (used in Theorem 9.3.4).

nodes.title: Theorem 2.7.3: Galois representations for weight 0 forms on GL_2 over a quadratic extension of a totally real field
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, K/F quadratic with Gal(K/F) = {1, τ}, and 𝛑 a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_K) of weight 0 (𝛑_v corresponds to φ_{0,1} at every infinite v of K) with trivial central character. Then there is a continuous irreducible ρ_{𝛑,p}: G_K → GL_2(Q̄_p) with WD(ρ_{𝛑,p}|_{G_{K_w}})^{ss} ≅ rec_p(𝛑_w ⊗ |·|^{−1/2})^{ss} for finite w ∤ p, equality of Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations when 𝛑_w is not a twist of Steinberg, and ρ_{𝛑,p}|_{G_{K_w}} Hodge–Tate with labelled weights (0,1) for w | p. (The paper prints GL_2(K) for GL_2(A_K) and G_{K_v} for G_{K_w}.)
hypotheses: F totally real, K/F quadratic (no condition on the signature of K).
proofSteps: For K CM this is a case of Mok's main theorem.

In general, Mok's §5.1 argument produces a cuspidal π of GSp_4(A_F) via Theorem 2.9.3 (the automorphic induction of 𝛑 ⊗ |·|); its infinity components lie in the L-packet of φ_{(2;1,0)} by Lemma 2.6.1 at real places of F split in K and by Mok Prop. 5.2 where K_v is complex; Mok §§5.2–5.3 then give ρ_{𝛑,p} as a constituent of ρ_{π,p}|_{G_K}.

sources.match: Attaches Galois representations to weight 0 cuspidal representations of GL_2 over any quadratic extension of a totally real field through GSp_4 over the totally real field, following Mok.

acceptance: For K totally real this recovers the Hilbert modular case.
Used in Theorem 9.3.4 for the local–global compatibility of the GL_2 form over KF'.

nodes.title: Theorem 9.3.1 (Theorem 1.1.3): every abelian surface over a totally real field is potentially automorphic
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real and A/F an abelian surface. Then 𝓡_A is potentially automorphic, and Conjecture 2.8.6 (meromorphic continuation and functional equation of Λ(H^i(A), s)) holds for A for each 0 ≤ i ≤ 4. In particular there is a finite Galois L/F such that 𝓡_A|_{G_L} is automorphic, and the L-function of H^1 over L is entire. Only challenging surfaces are shown potentially modular in the sense of Definition 9.1.8.
hypotheses: F totally real; Arthur's classification for GSp_4 in its conditional form (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.0, ML.4).
proofSteps: Since H^i = ∧^iH^1, ε(𝓡)ε(𝓡^∨) = N(𝓡) (Tate) and H^i^∨ = H^i(i), it suffices to treat i = 1, 2 and to prove (2.8.5).

By Brauer induction (Taylor, Remarks on a conjecture of Fontaine and Mazur, Corollary 2.2; InductionRestriction layer 6 and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5) it suffices to find a Galois totally real F'/F with 𝓡_A|_{G_{F''}} and ∧^2𝓡_A|_{G_{F''}} automorphic for every F'' ⊂ F' with Gal(F'/F'') solvable.

Types D, F: potentially abelian (Johansson Prop. 11, Lemma 14). Types B[C_1], C, E ≠ E[D_n]: 𝓡_A = 𝓡^1 ⊕ 𝓡^2, potentially automorphic by BLGGT Thm 5.4.1, descending along solvable extensions by BLGHT Lemma 1.3, and ∧^2𝓡_A = det𝓡^1 ⊕ det𝓡^2 ⊕ (𝓡^1 ⊗ 𝓡^2) is automorphic by Ramakrishnan's Theorem M (ML.5).

Types A, B[C_2], E[D_n]: Theorem 9.2.8, the proof of Proposition 9.2.1, Lemma 2.9.1, Theorem 2.9.3 and Lemma 8.3.2 make ρ_{A,p}|_{G_{F''}} irreducible, modular and automorphic; Henniart's refinement of Kim's exterior square transfer with Theorem 2.9.3 makes ∧^2ρ_{A,p} automorphic.
Remark 9.3.2: Kim–Henniart can be replaced by the degree 5 standard L-function of the GSp_4 form, but Theorem 2.9.3 remains essential.

sources.match: Proves potential automorphy of the compatible system of every abelian surface over a totally real field and the meromorphic continuation and functional equation of its L-functions, through Brauer induction and the potential modularity of challenging surfaces.

For A of type A the automorphic Π over L is cuspidal on GL_4.

nodes.title: Corollary 9.3.3 and Theorem 1.1.2: the Hasse–Weil conjecture for genus two curves and abelian surfaces
nodes.statement: Let C/F be a genus two curve over a totally real field, and Λ(C,s) = ∏_{i=0}^{2}Λ_i(C,s)^{(−1)^i} with Λ_1(C,s) = Λ_1(Jac(C),s). Then Λ(C,s) has meromorphic continuation to C and Λ(C,s) = εN^{−s}Λ(C, 2 − s) with ε ∈ R and N ∈ Q_{>0}. Consequently Conjecture 1.1.1 (Serre's form of the Hasse–Weil conjecture) holds for every genus two curve and every abelian surface over a totally real field (Theorem 1.1.2). Both versions of the paper print Λ(C, 3 − s); the symmetry of a curve's completed function is s ↦ 1 + dim C − s = 2 − s, while 3 − s belongs to Λ(Jac(C), s).
hypotheses: F totally real; C smooth projective geometrically connected of genus 2 over F.
proofSteps: Apply Theorem 9.3.1 to A = Jac(C) (JacobianChallenge layers D–F): H^1(C) = H^1(Jac C), so Λ_1(C,s) continues with its functional equation s ↦ 2 − s.
Λ_0(C,s) is the completed Dedekind zeta function of F and Λ_2(C,s) = Λ_0(C,s−1); they are exchanged by s ↦ 2 − s.
For abelian surfaces, Theorem 9.3.1 gives Conjecture 1.1.1 directly.

sources.locator: Corollary 9.3.3, §9.3, p. 259; Theorem 1.1.2 and Conjecture 1.1.1, §1.1, pp. 3–4
sources.match: Deduces the meromorphic continuation and functional equation of the completed Hasse–Weil function of a genus two curve from Theorem 9.3.1 applied to its Jacobian, which with Theorem 9.3.1 gives the Hasse–Weil conjecture for genus two curves and abelian surfaces.

acceptance: For C: y^2 = x^5 + 1 over Q the completed L-function of C is meromorphic with symmetry s ↦ 2 − s.
The curve functional equation must use the reflection 2−s; 3−s is the reflection parameter for the whole completed zeta function of the Jacobian, not for its H^1 L-function (which also uses 2−s).

nodes.title: Theorem 9.3.4 (Theorem 1.1.4): genus one curves over quadratic extensions of totally real fields are potentially modular
nodes.statement: Let K/F be a quadratic extension of a totally real F, and E/K a genus one curve or an elliptic curve. Then E is potentially modular. If End_K(E) = Z, there are a Galois extension of totally real fields F'/F and a weight 0 cuspidal 𝛑 on GL_2(A_{KF'}) with trivial central character such that ρ_{E,l}|_{G_{KF'}} ≅ ρ_{𝛑,l} for every l, with WD_v(ρ_{E,l}|_{G_{KF'_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec(𝛑_v ⊗ |det|_v^{−1/2}) at every finite v; and Conjecture 2.8.6 holds for E. If End_K(E) ≠ Z, E has CM defined over K and ρ_{E,l}|_{G_K} is a sum of two characters of algebraic Hecke characters, so no cuspidal 𝛑 exists; E is potentially modular in the sense of the first sentence. The printed 'more precisely' clause is stated for every E and fails in the CM case (K = Q(i), y^2 = x^3 − x).
hypotheses: F totally real; K/F quadratic of any signature.
proofSteps: Replace E by its Jacobian. CM case: modular through Hecke characters (CM.4). If E is isogenous to a twist of E^σ, argue as in Proposition 9.2.1 (type E[D_n]).
Otherwise A = Res_{K/F}E has type B[C_2] with 𝓡_A = Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}𝓡_E; Theorem 9.2.8 gives F'/F linearly disjoint from K/F and π on GSp_4(A_{F'}) with ρ_{A,p}|_{G_{F'}} ≅ ρ_{π,p}.

The transfer Π of π to GL_4(A_{F'}) satisfies Π ⊗ (κ∘Art∘det) ≅ Π for the quadratic character κ of K' = KF'/F', so Π is the automorphic induction of 𝛑 ⊗ |det| for a cuspidal 𝛑 on GL_2(A_{K'}) (Arthur–Clozel Chapter 3, Theorems 4.2 and 5.1; ML.5).
Lemma 2.6.1 and a Frobenius-eigenvalue density argument show 𝛑 has weight 0 and trivial central character; Theorem 2.7.3 gives the local–global compatibility.
