nodes.title: Proposition 9.4.1: the Hasse–Weil conjecture for Kummer surfaces
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian surface over a totally real F and X = Km(A) its Kummer surface (the minimal resolution of A/⟨−1⟩, a smooth projective K3 surface of geometric Picard number ≥ 17). Then Conjecture 1.1.1 holds for X. The same holds for any K3 surface over F with a Shioda–Inose structure over F. (Definition 9.4.2 and the rest of §9.4 — F-abelian varieties, K3 surfaces of Picard rank ≥ 17, Nori's fake Kummer surfaces — are discussion without further theorems.)
hypotheses: F totally real; A an abelian surface over F.
proofSteps: H^*(X, Q_p) vanishes in odd degrees; in even degrees it is generated by the image of H^*(A, Q_p)^{±1} (all of H^0, H^2, H^4 of A) and the 16 classes of the exceptional divisors over the 2-torsion points, a twist of an Artin representation (the permutation representation on A[2]). The cohomology of the Kummer construction is recorded as a gap (no atlas layer plans Kummer or K3 surfaces).
Theorem 9.3.1 handles the part from A, and the meromorphic continuation and functional equation of Artin L-functions (Brauer induction; AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4) the exceptional part.

sources.match: Deduces the Hasse–Weil conjecture for Kummer surfaces of abelian surfaces from Theorem 9.3.1 and Artin L-functions, and discusses further K3 surfaces.

acceptance: H^2(Km(A)) has dimension 22 = 6 + 16.
The exceptional classes contribute an Artin L-function up to a Tate twist.

nodes.title: Proposition 10.1.1 (Theorem 1.1.7): modularity of ordinary abelian surfaces
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real with p > 2 splitting completely, and A/F an abelian surface with good ordinary reduction at every v | p whose unit root crystalline eigenvalues at each v | p are distinct mod p. Assume A has a polarization of degree prime to p, that ρ̄_{A,p}: G_F → GSp_4(F_p) (the dual of A[p]) is vast and tidy, and that ρ̄_{A,p} is ordinarily modular: some π of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, ordinary at every v | p, has ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄_{A,p} and ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} pure for all finite v. Then A is modular: some ordinary π' of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 has ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ_{A,p}. The printed 'unramified and ordinary' is corrected to 'ordinary'. (Remark 10.1.2: without a polarization of degree prime to p, ρ̄_{A,p} is reducible, but need not land in any conjugate of GSp_4(F_p).)
hypotheses: As stated; F totally real, p > 2 totally split.
proofSteps: The polarization of degree prime to p puts ρ_{A,p} in GSp_4(Z_p) with multiplier ε^{−1} (AP.0); Proposition 2.8.1 (R11.5) gives purity at every finite place and finiteness of ramification.

Good ordinary reduction with distinct unit roots mod p gives p-distinguished weight 2 ordinarity at v | p: the connected–étale sequence of the p-divisible group (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 via AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4) gives the filtration, D_cris and the crystalline comparison (PadicHodgeTheory R06.2, CohomologyComparisons CP.2) give the unit roots, and Katz–Messing identifies them with the l-adic Frobenius data (requested at A4).
Theorem 8.4.1 applies.

sources.locator: Proposition 10.1.1 and Remark 10.1.2, §10.1, pp. 264–265; Theorem 1.1.7, §1.1, p. 5
sources.match: States and proves the modularity of an ordinary abelian surface with distinct unit roots, a polarization of degree prime to p, vast and tidy and ordinarily modular residual representation, as an immediate consequence of Theorem 8.4.1.

acceptance: The conclusion is modularity in the sense of Definition 9.1.8.
It is the input of Theorem 10.2.6 and Lemma 10.3.1.

nodes.title: Proposition 10.1.3: three cases in which ρ̄_p is ordinarily modular
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real with p > 2 splitting completely and ρ̄_p: G_F → GSp_4(F_p) absolutely irreducible with multiplier ε^{−1}, vast and tidy and p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary. Suppose (1) p = 3 and ρ̄_3 is induced from a 2-dimensional representation with inverse cyclotomic determinant over a totally real quadratic E/F in which 3 is unramified; or (2) p = 5 and ρ̄_5 is induced in the same way from a GL_2(F_5)-valued representation, 5 unramified in E; or (3) ρ̄_p is induced from a character of a quartic CM extension H/F in which p splits completely. Then ρ̄_p is ordinarily modular: some π of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, ordinary above p, has ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄_p and ρ_{π,p} pure at all finite places. The printed 'unramified and ordinary' is corrected to 'ordinary': in the très ramifiée cases the constructed π is of Steinberg type above p. Consequently in these cases the residual modularity hypothesis of Theorem 1.1.7 can be dropped.
hypotheses: As stated.
proofSteps: Cases (1)–(2): ρ̄ = Ind_{G_E}^{G_F}ϱ̄ with ϱ̄|_{G_{E(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible and ϱ̄ on inertia above p an extension of ε^{−1} by 1. Once ϱ̄ is modular, Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty (2013, Theorem A; OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.2) gives an ordinary Hilbert form of parallel weight 2 and trivial character, π is its automorphic induction from E to F (Roberts' theta lift, GSp_4 Part II), and purity comes from Blasius and Caraiani (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.3–R19.5).

ϱ̄ is modular: by Langlands–Tunnell with Tate's lifting when its projective image is solvable (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4–R17.5); by the odd Artin conjecture over totally real fields (Pilloni–Stroh) for p = 3 and projective image A_5; for surjective GL_2(F_5)-valued ϱ̄ by Khare–Wintenberger lifts, Kisin's lifting and Pilloni–Stroh (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.1).
Case (3): ρ̄ = Ind_{G_H}^{G_F}χ; take an algebraic Grössencharacter ψ of H of conductor prime to p with ψ_p ≡ χ (CM.4) and induce automorphically to GL_2 over the real quadratic E ⊂ H, then to F.

sources.locator: Proposition 10.1.3 and its proof, §10.1, pp. 265–267; §1.1 after Theorem 1.1.7, p. 6
sources.match: Establishes ordinary residual modularity for mod 3 and mod 5 representations induced from GL_2 over a real quadratic extension and for representations induced from characters of quartic CM fields, through automorphic induction and known rank 2 results.

acceptance: With Proposition 10.1.1 it gives modularity of ordinary surfaces whose mod 3 representation is induced from a real quadratic field.
Case (3) covers mod p representations of CM type.

nodes.title: Lemmas 7.5.25–7.5.27: crossing with dihedral extensions
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real with p split completely and K/F quadratic with p unramified. (7.5.25) There is a Galois H/F ⊃ K with D = Gal(H/F) dihedral of order 8, Gal(H/K) ≅ (Z/2)^2, H the Galois closure of a quadratic M/K, H/F unramified above p with ⟨Frob_v⟩ not central in D, and H/F linearly disjoint from any given extension disjoint from K/F. (7.5.26) For r̄: G_F → GL_2(F̄_p) absolutely irreducible with det r̄ = ε̄^{−1} and r̄|_{G_{F_v}} an extension of ε̄^{−1}χ_v^{−1} by an unramified χ_v at each v | p, K linearly disjoint from F(r̄), H as in 7.5.25 disjoint from F(r̄), and ρ̄ := Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}(r̄|_{G_K} ⊗ δ_{M/K}): ρ̄ is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary with multiplier ε̄^{−1}, ρ̄ ≅ V ⊗ U (V from r̄, U the faithful 2-dimensional representation of D) is absolutely irreducible, and ρ̄(G_F) = (Γ × D)/⟨(−1, [a,b])⟩ or Γ × D according as Γ = r̄(G_F) has a central element of order 2. (7.5.27) For p ≥ 5 with Γ = GL_2(F_p), or p = 5 and Γ the preimage of S_4 ⊂ S_5 ≅ PGL_2(F_5), G ∩ Sp_4(F_p) is enormous (weakly enormous if Γ = GL_2(F_5)), and ρ̄ is vast and tidy.
hypotheses: p unramified in K; the proof of 7.5.27 prints 'E' where F is meant.
p > 2; the character and distinctness arguments use odd residual characteristic.
proofSteps: 7.5.25: with K = F(√α), take β = x^2 − αy^2 a unit and non-residue at every v | p and H = F(√α, √β, √(x + y√α)); embedding problems with local conditions (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.4).
7.5.26: compute the induced representation as a tensor product with the dihedral representation; the local shape at v | p follows from the non-centrality of Frob_v.
7.5.27: the big-image criteria for subgroups of GSp_4 (Lemmas 7.5.18–7.5.19, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7).

For Γ = GL_2(F_5) the intersection with Sp_4 is weakly enormous but not enormous.

nodes.title: Theorem 10.1.4: modularity of elliptic curves over quadratic extensions via mod 5
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real with 5 split completely, K/F quadratic with 5 unramified, and E/K an elliptic curve with good ordinary or semistable ordinary reduction at every w | 5. Suppose (1) the projective image of ϱ̄_{E,5} is S_5 = PGL_2(F_5) or S_4, and (2) some r̄_5: G_F → GL_2(F_5) with det r̄_5 = ε̄^{−1} has r̄_5|_{G_K} ≅ ϱ̄_{E,5}. Then E is modular. In particular there are infinitely many modular elliptic curves over K, up to twist, without CM and not coming from a subfield of K; for example F = Q(√d), d a positive nonsquare integer with X^4−d irreducible and d ≡ 1,4 mod 5, K = Q(d^{1/4}), a field of mixed signature.
hypotheses: As stated.
proofSteps: Lemma 7.5.26 applied to r̄_5 gives ρ̄ = Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}(ϱ̄_{E,5} ⊗ δ_{M/K}), vast, tidy and 5-distinguished weight 2 ordinary (Lemma 7.5.27). Verify the disjointness required by Lemma 7.5.26: K/F is unramified at 5, while the possible determinant quadratic subfield of the residual extension is ramified at 5; the stated projective image rules out other quadratic projective quotients.

As in Proposition 10.1.3, r̄_5 comes from an ordinary Hilbert form over F; its base change to K (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4), twisted by δ_{M/K} and induced back to F, gives π of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, ordinary above 5, with ρ̄_{π,5} ≅ ρ̄ and ρ_{π,5} pure.
Theorem 8.4.1 makes Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}(ϱ_{E,5} ⊗ δ_{M/K}) modular, and the argument of Theorem 9.3.4 makes ϱ_{E,5} ⊗ δ_{M/K}, hence E, modular.

acceptance: The examples are not CM because their mod 5 representations are not projectively dihedral or cyclic.
The fields K need not be totally real or CM.

nodes.title: The Burkhardt quartic, the odd-theta cover P and its twists P(ρ̄)
nodes.statement: B := 𝒜_2(3), the moduli of principally polarized abelian surfaces with full level 3 structure; over C it is the complement of the Hessian in the Burkhardt quartic, it is rational over Q (Bruin–Nasserden), and PSp_4(F_3) acts on it. B(2) := 𝒜_2(6) → B is Galois with group S_6 ≅ PSp_4(F_2) = Sp_4(F_2), the identification fixed by the action on the six Weierstrass points of C with Jac(C) = A. P is the intermediate degree 6 cover for the point stabilizers S_5 ⊂ S_6, equivalently the moduli 𝒜_2(3)^− of principally polarized surfaces with a symmetric odd theta structure of level 3; a rational point of P in the image of the Torelli map is a Jacobian with a marked rational Weierstrass point, i.e. of a curve y^2 = f(x) with f quintic. The PSp_4(F_3)-action on P over Q(√−3) descends to Q for the étale group G of symplectic automorphisms of μ_3^2 × (Z/3)^2 modulo ±1. For ρ̄: G_F → GSp_4(F_3) with multiplier ε̄^{−1}, P(ρ̄) → B(ρ̄) is the twist by ρ̄ (B(ρ̄) the twisted moduli of AP.6 with n = 3). Proposition 10.2.3: there is a G-equivariant birational map P → P^3 over Q (the odd theta map of Dolgachev–Lehavi, birational by Bolognesi). Lemma 10.2.4: P(ρ̄) is rational over F.
hypotheses: ρ̄ has multiplier ε̄^{−1}; F a number field.
proofSteps: S_6 ≅ Sp_4(F_2): for a genus two curve with Weierstrass points r_1, …, r_6, the fifteen differences r_i − r_j are the nonzero points of A[2], and the Weil pairing of r_i − r_j and r_k − r_l is the parity of #({i,j} ∩ {k,l}) (BCGP25 §8.1.1); the identification is fixed with the point stabilizer S_5(b), distinct from the transitive S_5(a).

Proposition 10.2.3 reduces rationality of P(ρ̄) to that of the twist P^3(ρ̄) of P^3 by the class σ ↦ θ(ρ̄^∨(σ)·diag(ε^{−1}(σ), ε^{−1}(σ), 1, 1)) in H^1(F, PGL_4(Q̄)), θ induced by the action of Sp_4(F_3) on μ_3^2 × (Z/3)^2.

Lemma 10.2.4: PSp_4(F_3) is perfect with Schur multiplier of order 2, so its Schur cover is Sp_4(F_3) and θ: PSp_4(F_3) → PGL_4(Q̄) lifts to θ̃: Sp_4(F_3) → GL_4(Q̄) (TauCeti.IsProjectiveRep.cohomologyClass_eq_zero_iff with the Schur multiplier, InductionRestriction layer 7); the lift is unique because Sp_4(F_3) is perfect and commutators in GL_n depend only on images in PGL_n. So the class comes from H^1(F, GL_4(Q̄)) = 0 (Hilbert 90) and P^3(ρ̄) ≅ P^3.

nodes.title: Corollary 9.3.6 and Lemma 9.3.7 of BCGP25: ordinary local Jacobians at 3
nodes.statement: Work over Q_3 with ρ̄: G_{Q_3} → GSp_4(F_3) of multiplier ε̄^{−1}, with finite-flat dual ρ̄^∨ which is ordinary, with unramified rank-two étale quotient V̄ and multiplicative submodule its Cartier dual. (9.3.6) If an ordinary principally polarized abelian surface A_0/F_3 has A_0[3]^{ét} ≅ V̄ and mod 2 image in S_5(b), there is a genus two X/Q_3 with a rational Weierstrass point, Jac(X) good ordinary and residual H^1-representation ρ̄; if the characteristic-zero lift has distinct unit roots, this persists in a sufficiently small neighbourhood. (9.3.7) Every such ρ̄ arises in this way from a good ordinary 3-distinguished Jacobian whose curve has a Q_3-rational Weierstrass point. Here 3-distinguished means distinct unit roots in characteristic zero as in BCGP25, not distinct reductions as required by BCGP18. The seeds: for the nonscalar conjugacy classes of V̄, four explicit quintic curves over F_3 and their unramified quadratic twists; for scalar Frobenius −1 on V̄, the product of elliptic curves over F_3 of traces −1 and 2 (quartic (X^2 + X + 3)(X^2 − 2X + 3), mod 2 permutation of order 6 in S_5(b)), and for +1 its unramified quadratic twist (traces 1 and −2).
hypotheses: p = 3; ρ̄ ordinary with finite flat dual (it then comes from a finite flat group scheme over Z_3, unique by Raynaud since e = 1 < p − 1).
proofSteps: Use polarized lifting (BCGP25 Lemma 9.3.4, group-scheme rank 3^4) to lift the prescribed finite-flat 3-torsion model to a principally polarized ordinary A/Z_3. Uniqueness of the finite-flat model over Z_3 is Raynaud, since e=1<3−1. Remark 9.3.5 gives direct Jacobian lifting when the special fibre is already a smooth genus-two Jacobian; it does not turn a product special fibre into a Jacobian.

The mod-2 condition gives a point of P(ρ̄)(Q_3). Use Kisin local constancy to retain its residual 3-torsion and mod-2 action, good ordinarity and distinct characteristic-zero unit roots on a small open neighbourhood. Intersect with the dense Torelli open M_2^w(ρ̄) ⊂ P(ρ̄) (BCGP25 §9.2.1, p.192); this yields a Jacobian with a rational Weierstrass point even for product seeds. Its curve need not have good reduction although its Jacobian does.

Run through the nonscalar and scalar conjugacy classes of V̄ and certify their étale 3-torsion, not only the Frobenius quartic. For the scalar seed of elliptic traces −1 and 2, (a_1,a_2)=(1,4): the two unit roots are distinct in characteristic zero but both reduce to −1. Twisting gives the +1 scalar seed. These cases do not satisfy the residual-distinctness hypothesis of the 2018 lifting theorem.

If moreover, for every v | 3, P(ρ̄)(F_v) contains a point of an ordinary principally polarized surface (A[3] ≅ V(ρ̄)^∨ with an F_v-rational odd theta characteristic), the A may also be taken with good ordinary reduction at every v | 3. nodes.title: Lemma 10.3.2: motives attached to symplectic GL_4 forms, conditionally
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real. Assume the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture, the standard conjectures, the Hodge conjecture and the Tate conjecture (the last is used three times in the sketched proof but is missing from the printed hypotheses), and that the Galois representations of every cuspidal Π on GL_4(A_F) of infinity type φ_{2;1,0} at every v | ∞ form an irreducible weakly compatible system. Let Π be such a representation with rational Hecke eigenvalues, of symplectic type with multiplier |·|^2. Then there is a motive A/F attached to Π which is either (1) an abelian surface or (2) an abelian fourfold with End_F(A) containing an order in a quaternion algebra D/Q (a fake abelian surface). Conversely, assuming only standard automorphy conjectures, an abelian fourfold A/F with End_F(A) ⊗ Q = End_C(A) ⊗ Q an indefinite quaternion algebra gives such a Π.
hypotheses: The listed conjectures, including the Tate conjecture, as explicit hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use a motivic-realization form of Fontaine–Mazur, together with the standard conjectures, to obtain a pure motive whose p-adic realization contains the given rank-four system. Rational traces, semisimplicity, Brauer–Nesbitt and Tate identify an isotypic rational piece and force its endomorphism centre to be Q. The weak statement that a representation occurs somewhere in geometric cohomology is not alone enough.

The Hodge conjecture and a polarizable weight-one Hodge structure realize the piece as H^1 of a complex abelian variety. To descend, use the countability of its isogeny class versus the Aut(C/F)-orbit, pass to a finite extension of F, then use restriction of scalars and Faltings isogeny and idempotent splitting to extract the required F-abelian factor. The Tate conjecture identifies its H^1 motive, not just its complex Hodge numbers.

Albert classification with centre Q leaves type I (surface with endomorphism ring Z), type II (indefinite quaternion algebra), and type III (definite quaternion algebra, not excluded). For the converse, use the proved type-II Mumford–Tate case: at p splitting the quaternion algebra, H^1=V⊕V with dim V=4 and symplectic similitudes on V. Check the Frobenius polynomial is the square of the integral rational degree-four polynomial, with the inverse-cyclotomic multiplier; this requires the quaternionic polarization and rationality argument as well as Weil bounds.

gaps.detail: Independent exact arithmetic verifies the corrected discriminant and point counts at both primes above 11 (recorded in AP.7/fake-surface-examples). The authors’ public Magma script and output at commit 8a274357327de5c326f6d1887998f2d6c5207659 contain Frobenius computations for another displayed model, but no list of candidate quadratic CM extensions of Q(√−6), unramified outside the stated bad primes, or a certificate eliminating every candidate. Expected Lemma 10.4.4 additionally needs the real-point and open-image proof beyond its source sketch.
